## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One fix is needed: `README.md:3` still says requests time out after 30 seconds, but this pull request changes the default to 60, so users reading the docs get the wrong default. This review traced `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` from `app/cli.py:3` into the `--timeout` argument at `app/cli.py:8` and read the parser tests. It found no correctness or silent-failure defects in the parser change. The updated `test_defaults` in `tests/test_cli.py:8` checks the new default through `parse_args([])`, and `test_explicit_options` in `tests/test_cli.py:14-15` still covers the explicit `--timeout` override. This review read the tests but did not run them.

## Changes
The pull request raises `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` in `app/cli.py` from 30 to 60 seconds and updates the default-value assertion in `tests/test_cli.py`. It also adds a one-line `review.txt` file at the repository root.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- README.md:3 — comments — Update the README default timeout to 60 seconds — Because `app/cli.py:3` now sets `DEFAULT_TIMEOUT = 60`, the README line "Requests time out after 30 seconds unless you pass `--timeout SECONDS`." is now false. `parse_args([])` returns `timeout == 60`, as the updated test at `tests/test_cli.py:8` asserts, and the README is not part of the diff. — Users who read the README expect a 30-second timeout when the CLI waits 60 seconds, so they may pass `--timeout` for no reason or misdiagnose slow failures.
